commonPoints: Carbon fiber damps vibration and weighs less; aluminum is cheaper
The 45 MP sensor shows small vibrations, so stiffness matters more than usual
Keep the center column down or skip it
Pick a load rating above camera plus heaviest lens
A fluid head is better than a ball head for video pans

ourGain.point: Canon kit weights: R5 738 g; + RF 24-70 F2.8L (900 g) = 1,638 g; + RF 70-200 F2.8L (1,070 g) = 1,808 g; + RF 100-500 with ring (1,530 g) = 2,268 g (5.0 lb). Every stills pick is rated 15-16 kg, about 6.6-7x the heaviest kit, so load is not the decider; leg stiffness and height are.

Five sections are not the problem, thin tubes are: a DPReview R5 reply warns thin 5-section legs end near 10 mm; the 5-section Tortoise 35C's thinnest tube is 18.4 mm (32.4 mm top) per Benro, and the LS-324CX ends at 22 mm.

Chooser by use: 45 MP landscapes and one tripod for everything = Tortoise 35C; RF 100-500 and tall users = Mach3 TMA38CL; wind and low angles = LS-324CX; long hikes with an own head = AM-284; 8K pans and a rigged R5 = SmallRig AD-01.
Front-heavy RF 70-200 creeping on a ball head: mount long lenses by the tripod ring, use a 40 mm-class ball (GX35, LH-40) and set friction before loosening.

painPoints.pain: Thin five-section travel legs are not stable enough for an R5 with a big zoom
painPoints.details: A DPReview R5 thread reply says small 5-section models end in leg sections around 10 mm, too thin for a heavy-ish full-frame camera with a large zoom.

quotes.text: usually the thinnest leg sections are around 10mm diameter and simply not stable enough for a heavy-ish FF camera with large zoom

painPoints.pain: Load ratings do not say how stable a tripod is
painPoints.details: The same DPReview reply says there is no standard for tripod and head load ratings.

quotes.text: completely ignore the stated load ratings - there is no standard

painPoints.pain: A light travel tripod shakes in wind with an R5 and RF 70-200
painPoints.details: A CameraEgg forum owner lost long exposures at Joshua Tree with an R5 and RF 70-200 f/2.8 on a Befree.

quotes.text: the whole thing just felt so flimsy in the wind and I ended up with blurry shots

painPoints.pain: The ball head creeps with a front-heavy RF 70-200
painPoints.details: A Canon Rumors R5 travel-tripod reply warns that a 70-200 gets front-heavy and the head must not creep.

quotes.text: A 70-200mm can get a bit front-heavy

painPoints.pain: Manfrotto's own clamp does not take Arca-Swiss L-brackets and lens feet
painPoints.details: The DPReview R5 reply notes Manfrotto used a proprietary clamp while cheap L-brackets and long lens plates come in Arca-Swiss.

painPoints.pain: Salt spray seizes twist locks on coastal trips
painPoints.details: A CameraEgg forum R5 owner rinses the leg locks every night on coastal trips or they grind and seize.

quotes.text: you have to rinse the leg locks in the shower every single night or they will start grinding and eventually seize up
